item: A08 Merge RNA weighting paragraphs
before:
The usefulness of a correction can differ between transcripts. A common amplitude may preserve a strong response change but also carry weak or inconsistent changes into other readouts. WitnessCell instead compares endpoint-eliminated responses in two disjoint halves of the training cells. A transcript with weaker agreement receives a smaller correction. Because the weights depend only on training measurements, the held-out combinations provide a separate test of whether this adjustment improves prediction.

Agreement between cell halves estimates sampling consistency in the available training measurements and determines the amplitude applied to each transcript. A training-selected uniform shrinkage control tests whether transcript-specific weighting adds value beyond reducing the correction by one common factor. Methods specifies the measurement scope of this consistency estimate.
after: The usefulness of a correction can differ between transcripts. A common amplitude may preserve a strong response change but also carry weak or inconsistent changes into other readouts. WitnessCell compares endpoint-eliminated responses in two disjoint halves of the training cells and assigns smaller corrections to transcripts with weaker agreement. This agreement measures sampling consistency within the source experiment. A training-selected uniform shrinkage control tests whether transcript-specific weighting adds value beyond reducing all corrections by one factor. Held-out combinations then provide a separate test of the training-derived adjustment; Methods specifies the measurement scope.

item: A09 Merge RNA concentration and sensitivity interpretation
before:
The largest benefits concerned a defined group of strongly changing readouts. Ten transcripts, including S100A9, S100A8, S100A12 and LYZ, accounted for over 90% of positive error reductions. Removing that fixed set or standardizing by training-condition variance eliminated the aggregate gain (Fig. 5e,f). Outside the set, shrinkage substantially reduced the harm caused by the unweighted correction, leaving the net gain close to zero and slightly negative. The useful RNA correction was therefore concentrated in a small subset of measured responses.

These sensitivity analyses distinguish effect size from breadth. Original-scale error emphasizes larger discrepancies; variance standardization changes readout weights; deletion tests the benefit outside the selected transcripts. Together, they locate the responsive readouts and establish how their magnitude contributes to overall improvement.
after: The largest benefits concerned a defined group of strongly changing readouts. Ten transcripts, including S100A9, S100A8, S100A12 and LYZ, accounted for over 90% of positive error reductions. Removing that fixed set or standardizing by training-condition variance eliminated the aggregate gain (Fig. 5e,f). These checks distinguish magnitude from breadth: standardization reduces the influence of large-scale discrepancies, while deletion tests prediction outside the selected transcripts. Outside that set, shrinkage substantially reduced the harm caused by the unweighted correction, leaving the net gain close to zero and slightly negative. Thus, its useful RNA improvement was concentrated, while its reduction of adverse corrections extended to other readouts.
